prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1498; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, scene photos and written statements from two witnesses. All three describe the same sequence: the insured stopped at the light and the following vehicle made contact at moderate speed. The other driver confirmed the account by phone and admitted to following too closely.

Entry 3: Rear bumper, trunk lid and tail light assembly damage on the insured vehicle is consistent with the described impact height and direction. Photos show no sign of older repairs or prior damage in the affected areas. Records confirm the policy was in force well before the loss, with no indication of earlier damage to the vehicle.

Entry 4: Confirmed that the driver of the insured vehicle lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy terms. Coverage question is closed. Position of the claimant within the vehicle at impact is not fully clear from the statements and photos, and counsel has been asked to clarify this.

Entry 5: Medical records received through counsel show a wrist fracture treated with immobilization and follow-up visits. Treatment followed a typical course, and visit frequency tapered as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same area appears in the records obtained.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has stayed consistent across the first contact, recorded statement and follow-up conversation with counsel present. The injury description fits the kind and force of the collision. Reserve reviewed and file remains open pending the claimant's response on seating position and the final medical summary.
